Deep Learning in Natural Language Processing: An Empirical Survey Modern Natural Language Processing has evolved significantly with the introduction of self-attention mechanisms and transformer neural networks. Transformer architectures replace recurrent neural networks by parallelizing sequence processing through multi-head self-attention mechanisms. Lightweight language models such as Google FLAN-T5-small provide an efficient alternative to multi-billion parameter models, achieving strong instruction-following performance while operating comfortably on standard consumer CPUs without dedicated GPU hardware acceleration. Vector similarity search enables semantic retrieval by calculating the inner product or cosine similarity between dense embeddings generated by models such as all-MiniLM-L6-v2. This allows systems to retrieve semantically related concepts even when exact query terms differ.
